notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence: NRHP nomination, a handful of Bulletin and annual-report items, roster and LighthouseFriends. Annual reports before 1891 are not in the corpus, so the 1871-1890 chapters rest on the nomination and LighthouseFriends (2, copyrighted; paraphrased). No newspaper pages were read. Disagreements stated in text: lens order (4th NRHP/USLHS vs 5th LF); light colour (red from start per NRHP vs white-to-red 30 Apr 1894 per LF); caisson diameter (25 ft plan vs 28 ft Burgess recollection); keeper name Bohm (roster/NRHP) vs Bohn (1935 Bulletin, likely OCR or print error). Bulletin items: Davis's rescue is in the 1917 volume (PDF page 52), 'November 3' year inferred from his 1917-1920 tenure; Stacey's 'December 20' is in the 1936 volume, so may be December 1935. LF says Grieder became keeper in 1930; roster lists him assistant 1931-34 and the 1931 Bulletin calls him assistant keeper. Sarah Jane Atwood (assistant 1874-78) is not linked in the prose to the keeper's wife in the 1875 ice story (LF says only 'his wife'). Ownership: Lighthouse Digest Nov/Dec 2019 says GSA transferred it in September 2019; the NRHP (2014) still gives USCG as owner. Salter's story is from his own account as relayed by the NRHP and LF, not read directly. Focal height 10.7 m = 35 ft; tower height 14.3 m (47 ft) per NRHP. Plymouth in Reamy's other_stations has no id because the Bulletin says only 'Plymouth'. The 1875 newspaper (Willimantic Journal, OCR, a reprinted telegram) names no revenue steamer; the Gallatin and pint-of-water details are LighthouseFriends only. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Davis's boat name is garbled OCR ('PIVmottth'); the story no longer names it. 1919 report says $11,000 was 'allotted', not spent.
